entries.html:
/t͡ʃerˈka.re/

Verb

  1. to look for
  2. to try [with di (+ infinitive)]

Inherited from Late Latin circāre, from Latin circa, circus.

Verb

  1. (intransitive) to return, to come back
  2. (intransitive) to return, to reappear
  3. (intransitive) to start (doing something again) [with a (+ infinitive)]
  4. (intransitive) to be (healthy, beautiful, clean, etc.) again
  5. (intransitive) to add up correctly (of an account)
  6. (transitive, literary) to return, to give back
  7. (transitive, literary) to turn (one's face, etc.)

Inherited from Latin tornāre (“to turn”).

/kon.ti.nuˈa.re/ · /kon.tiˈnwa.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) to continue, to keep on doing (an action)
  2. (transitive) to continue, to resume (an action)
  3. (intransitive) to continue, to last (of a thing) [auxiliary avere or essere]
  4. (intransitive) to continue, to persevere, to carry on (of a person) [auxiliary avere]

Borrowed from Latin continuāre, from continuus.

/kos.truˈi.re/

Verb

  1. to build, construct
  2. to plan, frame

From Latin cōnstruere, probably a borrowing.

/komˈprɛn.de.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) to comprise, to include, to encompass
  2. (transitive) to understand, comprehend, take the point, get the point
    1. Synonyms: capire, intendere

From Latin comprendere, variant of comprehendere.

/semˈbra.re/

Verb

  1. to seem, to look (like), to appear
  2. to sound, taste or feel (like)
  3. (impersonal) to seem

Borrowed from Old Occitan semblar, from Late Latin similāre, a verb based on Latin similis (“similar”). More or less a doublet of somigliare.

/penˈsa.re/

Verb

  1. to think
  2. (transitive) to think about someone
  3. to realize
  4. to expect

Inherited from Latin pēnsāre (“weigh carefully”), frequentative of pendere. Doublet of pesare.

/moˈri.re/

Noun m.

  1. death

Verb

  1. (intransitive) to die [auxiliary essere]
    1. Synonyms: (euphemistic) andare agli alberi pizzuti, (euphemistic) andare all'altro mondo, crepare, decedere, defungere, lasciarci la pelle, lasciarci le cuoia, lasciarci le penne, (euphemistic) mancare, (euphemistic) passare a miglior vita, procombere, schiattare, tirare le cuoia, (euphemistic) trapassare, (euphemistic) venire meno, (euphemistic) volare in cielo
  2. (obsolete or Tuscany, transitive) to kill [auxiliary avere]; (normally only participially)
    1. Synonym: uccidere

Inherited from Latin morī(rī).

/teˈne.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) to hold
    1. to set aside; to conserve
    2. to hold (one's spot in line, etc.)
    3. to reserve
  2. (transitive) to keep
  3. (ambitransitive) to hold up; to sustain
  4. (transitive) continue to wear; to not remove (a garment); to keep on (a garment)
  5. (transitive) to take
  6. (transitive, chiefly southern Italy) to have; to possess
    1. Synonym: avere
  7. (transitive) to treat (in a certain way)
  8. (transitive) to have employed
  9. (transitive) to manage
  10. (transitive) to carry out (of a speech, lesson, etc.)
  11. (transitive) to have over or keep (at a place)
  12. (transitive) to hold back (an impulse, feeling, etc.)
  13. (transitive) to look over or take care of
  14. (transitive) to assume or take up (a behavior, attitude, etc.)
  15. (transitive) to take up (to occupy space)
  16. (transitive, informal) to contain
  17. (transitive, military) to defend (a position, etc.) from enemy attack
  18. (transitive, journalism) to continue coverage of uninteresting or unpressing news, in hopes of future developments
  19. (transitive, literary) to consider or deem; to hold to be
  20. (transitive, archaic) to refrain from spending; to be stingy
  21. (intransitive) to stick or attach well [auxiliary avere] (of a glue, etc.)
  22. (intransitive) to be airtight [auxiliary avere]
  23. (intransitive) to seem colorable; to hold water [auxiliary avere]
  24. (intransitive) to last [auxiliary avere]
  25. (intransitive) to support someone's views, positions, etc. [with per] [auxiliary avere]
  26. (intransitive) to root [with per ‘for’] [auxiliary avere]
  27. (intransitive) to like or love (in a non romantic way) [with a] [auxiliary avere]
  28. (intransitive, economics) to remain stable [auxiliary avere] (of a currency, stock market, etc.)
  29. (intransitive, rare) to look like [auxiliary avere]

Usage Note

  1. The use of tenere in the sense of avere (“to have”) is typically nonstandard and often associated with the Neapolitan dialect, and region.

Inherited from Latin tenēre, from Proto-Italic *tenēō, stative from Proto-Indo-European *ten- (“to stretch, draw”).

See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

/proˈdur.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) to produce, yield, bear, generate
  2. (transitive) to produce, manufacture, make
    1. Synonym: fabbricare
  3. (transitive) to cause, produce

Borrowed from Latin prōdūcere.

/perˈmet.te.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) to allow, to let, to permit, to authorize, to entitle
    1. Synonyms: consentire, autorizzare, lasciare

From Latin permittere.

/ˈkje.de.re/ · /ˈkjɛ.de.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) to ask (for)
  2. (transitive) to ask, request
  3. (intransitive) to ask [with di ‘about (someone)’] [auxiliary avere]

Inherited from Latin quaerere, with dissimilation of /r–r/ to /d–r/.

/rap.pre.zenˈta.re/

Verb

  1. to be, constitute, represent, account for, symbolize, mean
    1. Synonyms: essere, costituire, significare, simboleggiare
  2. to represent, depict, portray, picture, show
    1. Synonym: mostrare
  3. to represent, act for, stand for, speak for, act as agent for, be
  4. (theater) to act, play, stage, give
  5. (film) to run, show

From Latin repraesentāre.

/de.diˈka.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) to dedicate

Derived from Latin dēdicāre.

/ri.korˈda.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) to remember, to recall, to recollect
  2. (transitive) to remind
  3. (transitive) to commemorate
    1. Synonym: commemorare
  4. (transitive) to mention, to record
    1. Synonyms: menzionare, nominare

From Latin recordārī.

/ˈsta.re/

Verb

  1. to stay, remain
    1. Synonyms: restare, rimanere
  2. to keep, stick [with a]
    1. Synonym: attenersi
  3. (followed by a gerund) to be doing something (present continuous)
  4. to be up to [with a]
    1. Synonyms: toccare, spettare
  5. to be about to [with per]
  6. (mathematics) to be in relation to, to stand in relation to (in English idiom applicable to statements of analogy and/or of mathematical relationship: "to be to") [with a]
  7. (regional) to live
    1. Synonyms: vivere, abitare
  8. to be in a certain condition
    1. Synonym: essere

Usage Note

  1. sta' + mi = stammi
  2. sta' + ti = statti
  3. sta' + gli = stagli
  4. sta' + le = stalle
  5. sta' + ci = stacci
  6. sta' + ne = stanne

Inherited from Latin stāre. Cognate with Spanish estar and English state.

/par.te.t͡ʃiˈpa.re/

Verb

  1. (intransitive) to take part in, to participate in, to share [auxiliary avere]
    1. Synonym: prendere parte
  2. (intransitive) to attend, to be present [auxiliary avere]
    1. Synonym: essere presente
  3. (transitive) to inform, to acquaint
    1. Synonym: annunciare

From Latin participāre.

/mi.liˈta.re/

Adjective

  1. military
  2. army

Noun m.

  1. serviceman

Verb

  1. to serve as a soldier, to militate
  2. (figurative) to fight [with a ‘for (an idea)’]
  3. to participate actively (in a political party or organization)
  4. to militate [with a favore di ‘in favor of (an argument or fact)’]

Probably borrowed from Latin mīlitāris.

From Latin mīlitāre.

/kos.ti.tuˈi.re/

Verb

  1. to constitute, establish, set up, form
    1. Synonyms: fondare, stabilire
  2. to constitute, compose, make up, consist
    1. Synonyms: formare, comporre
  3. to constitute, represent, be
    1. Synonyms: rappresentare, essere
  4. to constitute, appoint, make
    1. Synonym: nominare

From Latin cōnstituō (“to set up, establish, confirm”).

Verb

  1. to happen, to occur

Adjective

  1. (relational) future

Noun m.

  1. future
  2. prospects
  3. (rare, literary) posterity

From Latin advenīre.

/ˈpor.re/

Verb

  1. to put
    1. Synonym: mettere
  2. to set, to place
    1. Synonym: collocare
  3. to lay down
    1. Synonym: posare
  4. to pose (a question, etc.)

Inherited from Latin pōnere (“to put, place”), with pōnō > *ponjo> *pogno > pongo subsumed to the 'L-pattern' of vengo (cf. Old Italian vegno, vegnamo, vegnono) in a much-debated process of 'velar allomorphy'. This is mirrored in Spanish pongo, vengo, but with an opposite outcome in Portuguese ponho, venho.

/ˈpɛr.de.re/

Verb

  1. (ambitransitive) to lose [auxiliary avere]
  2. to waste
  3. to destroy
  4. to miss, to be late for something

Inherited from Latin perdere. The variant past participle perso was created by analogy with preso, etc.

/eˈzis.te.re/

Verb

  1. (intransitive) to exist, to be

From Latin exsistere.

/uʃˈʃi.re/

Verb

  1. (intransitive) to go out, leave, exit
  2. (intransitive) to get off, get out
  3. (intransitive) to disappear
  4. (intransitive) to flow, run (of a liquid)
  5. (intransitive) to descend, spring (from)
  6. (intransitive) to release, come out (be published)
  7. (intransitive) to date
  8. (vulgar, slang) to "get it/them out" (to show body parts by taking off clothes, especially for erotic purposes)
    1. in the form "uscirle", literally "to get them out": to show the breasts
    2. in the form "uscirlo", literally "to get it out": to show the penis
    3. in the form "escile", literally "get them out": invitation to a woman to show her breasts
    4. in the form "escilo", literally "get it out": invitation to a man to show his penis

From older escire, from Latin exīre, from ex + eō (“to go”). The word may have been phonetically influenced by the etymologically unrelated uscio (“door”).

Compare Sicilian nèsciri, Catalan eixir, Romanian ieși, Old Spanish exir and Old French issir.

/la.voˈra.re/

Verb

  1. (intransitive) to work; to labor
    1. Synonyms: esercitare, svolgere, occuparsi, professare, operare, agire, ingegnarsi, adoperarsi, impegnarsi
  2. (intransitive) to work; to function
    1. Synonyms: funzionare, produrre
  3. (intransitive) to run or operate (a business, etc.); to do business
  4. (transitive) to work or carve (a material)
    1. Synonyms: trattare, manipolare, elaborare, scolpire, intarsiare, sbalzare
  5. (transitive) to knead (dough)
  6. (transitive) to cultivate
    1. Synonyms: dissodare, coltivare
  7. (transitive, rare) to butter up or wheedle
    1. Synonym: lavorarsi

From Latin labōrāre.

/diˈri.d͡ʒe.re/

Verb

  1. to address (a letter etc.)
  2. to run, manage or direct
  3. to lead
  4. to conduct (an orchestra)

From Latin dīrigere (“to steer, direct”), probably borrowed in this form.

/de.fiˈni.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) to define
  2. (transitive) to decide, to resolve

Derived from Latin dēfīnīre (“to bound, set bounds to; to limit; to define, explain, designate by limiting”). By surface analysis, de- +‎ finire.

/skoˈpri.re/

Verb

  1. to uncover
  2. to discover, find out
  3. to sight; to spot

From s- +‎ coprire (“cover”).

/riˈt͡ʃe.ve.re/

Verb

  1. to receive, get, have, be given, take
    1. Synonyms: avere, ottenere, prendere, percepire, provare
  2. to accept
    1. Synonym: accettare
  3. to accommodate, hold, receive, welcome, meet, see, shelter
    1. Synonyms: accogliere, ospitare, contenere, vedere, incontrare
  4. (radio, television, etc.) to receive, pick up, read
    1. Synonym: prendere

From Latin recipere. Possibly borrowed from a Gallo-Italic language, where Latin /-p-/ > /v/ is a regular change, unlike in Italian. Compare the doublet recepire.

/utˈt͡ʃi.de.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) to kill
    1. Synonyms: ammazzare, assassinare

From Old Italian occidere, from Latin occīdō (“to kill, slay”). Compare Romanian ucide.

/in.diˈka.re/

Verb

  1. to point out, point to
  2. to show, to mean, to signpost, to mark
    1. Synonym: mostrare
  3. to recommend, to advise
    1. Synonyms: consigliare, richiedere
  4. to indicate
    1. Synonym: dire

From Latin indicāre.

/pre.veˈde.re/

Verb

  1. to foresee, to anticipate
  2. to forecast
  3. to plan
  4. to include
    1. Synonym: includere

Usage Note

  1. The conjugation of this verb differs from vedere in having an alternative, regularly formed future and conditional prevederò etc.

From Latin praevidēre.

/mosˈtra.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) to show
    1. Synonym: fare vedere
  2. (transitive) to indicate, to point
  3. (transitive) to explain, to reveal, to demonstrate
  4. (intransitive, rare) to pretend

Inherited from Latin mōnstrāre (“to show”). Cognate with Spanish mostrar, Occitan muishar and French montrer.

/komˈpor.re/

Verb

  1. to compose, compound
  2. to constitute, form
  3. to dial (a telephone)
  4. to arrange, adjust
  5. to settle, patch up (a disagreement)
  6. to typeset

Noun m.

  1. (music) composition

From Latin compōnere.

/fonˈda.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) to found, establish, constitute, start, set up, build
    1. Synonyms: avviare, costituire
  2. (transitive, figurative) to found, base, ground
    1. Synonym: basare

Inherited from Latin fundāre.

/aˈpri.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) to open
    1. Synonyms: schiudere, dischiudere
  2. (transitive) to unlock
  3. (transitive) to turn on

From Latin aperīre. Compare Sicilian ràpiri.

/ko.minˈt͡ʃa.re/

Verb

  1. (ambitransitive) to begin, to start, to commence, to set about
    1. Synonyms: incominciare, iniziare, (dated, regional) principiare

Inherited from Vulgar Latin *cominitiāre.

/ˈzvɔl.d͡ʒe.re/

Verb

  1. to unroll, unwind
    1. Synonyms: srotolare, sciogliere
  2. to develop
    1. Synonyms: elaborare, sviluppare
  3. to discuss
  4. to carry out
    1. Synonyms: esercitare, realizzare

From s- +‎ volgere; cognate with Piedmontese svòlge.

/fiˈni.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) to finish [auxiliary avere]
  2. (intransitive) to end up (doing something) [with per (+ infinitive); or with con, along with il or lo or l' (+ infinitive)] [auxiliary avere]
  3. (intransitive) to finish, to end [auxiliary essere]
  4. (intransitive) to end up (somewhere) [auxiliary essere]

Inherited from Latin fīnīre.

/zvi.lupˈpa.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) to develop
  2. (intransitive, informal) to mature (of a plant or animal), to reach puberty (of an adolescent)

From s- +‎ viluppo (“tangle”) +‎ -are. Compare Piedmontese svilupé.

/kon.teˈne.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) to contain

From Latin continēre.

/ˈkre.de.re/

Verb

  1. to believe
  2. to think

Conjugation

  1. Unlike all other verbs, the negative imperative second person plural of credere may take the subjunctive rather than the indicative in some contexts, although the indicative is also used in others:

Inherited from Latin crēdere (“to believe”).

/forˈma.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) to form, create, shape, make, mould/mold
    1. Synonyms: creare, dare forma, fare, modellare
  2. (transitive) to form, establish, set up, create, make up
    1. Synonyms: creare, costituire, fondare
  3. (transitive) to train, educate
    1. Synonym: istruire

From Latin formāre.

/ap.paˈri.re/

Verb

  1. to appear
    1. Synonym: comparire
  2. to seem, to look
    1. Synonyms: parere, sembrare
  3. to grow

From Latin appārēre, from ad- + pāreō. Compare Sicilian appàrriri.

/re.d͡ʒisˈtra.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) to register, record, note
    1. Synonym: annotare
  2. (transitive) to record, tape, video
  3. (transitive) to adjust, set
    1. Synonyms: regolare, aggiustare
  4. (transitive) to check in

From registro +‎ -are.

/d͡ʒoˈka.re/

Verb

  1. to play, specifically:
    1. (intransitive) to play a game, for fun or as a pastime
    2. (intransitive) to do something for fun
    3. (intransitive) to partake in a sport or game
    4. (intransitive) to act as required from a game
    5. (intransitive) to participate in a sporting match
    6. (transitive) to put into action (in a game)
  2. (intransitive, hunting) to respond to bait (of birds)
  3. (intransitive) to have a gambling addiction
  4. (transitive) to put as stake (in a game)
    1. (by extension) to bet, wager
  5. (transitive) to spend or waste (time) playing
  6. (figurative, transitive) to deceive or manipulate
  7. (figurative, intransitive):
    1. (with di) to use (something) skillfully
    2. (mechanical engineering) to have backlash (of a mechanism)
    3. to be important, to matter
    4. to make the most of, to take advantage of

Inherited from Latin iocārī. By surface analysis, gioco (“game”) +‎ -are. Cognate with Sicilian jucari.

/ok.kuˈpa.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) to occupy, take over, squat in
    1. Synonyms: prendere possesso, impossessarsi
  2. (transitive) to occupy, take up, fill
    1. Synonyms: impegnare, riempire, ricoprire
  3. (transitive) to employ, find a job
    1. Synonyms: impiegare, impiegarsi

Borrowed from Latin occupāre.

/ofˈfri.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) to offer, treat

From Vulgar Latin *offerīre, from Latin offerre.

/gare/ · /leˈɡa.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) bind, tie
  2. (transitive) unite
  3. (transitive) connect, link
  4. (transitive, rare) alloy
  5. (intransitive) unite, bind, bond, fuse, join together
  6. (intransitive) get along (with someone)
  7. (transitive) bequeath
  8. (transitive, archaic or rare) dispatch as a delegation

Inherited from Latin ligāre.

Borrowed from Latin lēgāre.

/senˈti.re/

Verb

  1. to feel
  2. to hear
  3. to smell

Inherited from Latin sentīre.
